description: You are given two strings of equal length s1 and s2, and a string baseStr. s1[i] and s2[i] are equivalent characters. Return the lexicographically smallest equivalent string of baseStr by using the equivalency information from s1 and s2.
intuition: Characters linked by equivalence form groups - Union-Find handles this perfectly. The trick is always making the lexicographically smallest character the group representative, so looking up any character instantly gives you its smallest equivalent.
approach: Use Union-Find where equivalent characters are unioned. Always make the lexicographically smallest character the root. For each character in baseStr, find its root to get the smallest equivalent.
explanation:
1. Union-Find with 26 nodes for a-z.
2. For each pair (s1[i], s2[i]), union their character indices.
3. Always make the smaller index the root to ensure lexicographic order.
4. For each character in baseStr, find its root to get the smallest equivalent.
5. Build and return the result string.
timeComplexity: O(n + m) where n is length of s1/s2 and m is length of baseStr
hints: Use Union-Find to group equivalent characters.
Always make the lexicographically smallest character the representative.
For each character in baseStr, find its representative.
